title: Sleeve agents: a named, role-bound home for a machine's local agent
objective:
A sleeve agent is a local agent (Claude Code, for now) that does machine-oriented work on one host, as the user: system administration, operations, documentation of the machine. Today it runs from `$HOME`, where it has no instruction file, no project-layer permissions, a memory slot shared with every other home-launched session, and leaves the harness's files loose in the home directory.

This thread gives a sleeve agent a home: `$MOLT_AGT_DIR/<host>-<role>/`, declared in the sleeve's manifest as an `[[agent]]` entry, rendered by Molt from a role profile kept in the user config repo, holding its role contract, its permissions and its memory. The harness's own state leaves `$HOME` for `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claude`, nothing recreates `~/.claude`, and a Claude launched with its cwd in `$HOME` is refused at its first prompt. Project agents (sessions run inside an Intent project, such as molt-vc) are out of scope: the project and Intent already bound them.
context:
## Where this came from

hv, 21 Oct 2026, to kovacs-sysadm and molt-vc: a local agent on kovacs runs out of `$HOME`, leaves LLM files there, and is "a bit too risky for my liking". The ask: a way, in Molt, to install, name, configure and manage a local agent safely. kovacs-sysadm surveyed kovacs; molt-vc verified the Claude Code facts the design turns on (docs, plus one live test on rhadamanth). hv's rulings are below; the thread is specified by molt-vc, built by molt-cc and molt-dc, and the kovacs move is planned by kovacs-sysadm and executed by hv.

## Three layers

| Layer         | Where                                        | Owned by       | Holds                                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Role source   | Molt-matts `config/agents/roles/<role>/`     | hv, in git     | the role contract (`AGENTS.md`) and permission profile (`settings.json`) templates            |
| Agent home    | `$MOLT_AGT_DIR/<host>-<role>/`               | Molt, rendered | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `memory/`, `work/`; the agent's cwd        |
| Harness state | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claude` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) | Claude Code    | credentials, transcripts, plugins, user settings; one per machine, shared by every session   |

The agent home is both the agent's config and its runtime directory: Claude Code's project-layer config is whatever sits in the cwd's `.claude/`, so cwd and config home coincide by construction. `autoMemoryDirectory` pins memory to `<home>/memory/`, so an agent's memory travels with its home rather than under the harness state's per-project directory, which Claude Code keys by git repository, or by the project root outside one, so that every session started from `$HOME` shares one.

## Naming and roles (hv, 21 Oct)

- Sleeve agents are always `<hostname>-<role>`: `rhadamanth-sysadm`, `kovacs-ops`.
- Roles, normalised across rhadamanth, gyges and kovacs: `sysadm` (system administration; may change the machine; cannot be sandboxed), `ops` (operations and monitoring; observe and diagnose, writes only inside its home; sandbox on), `docs` (documentation; sandbox on).
- `MOLT_AGT_DIR` follows `MOLT_PRJ_DIR` and `MOLT_CFG_DIR`; default `$HOME/Devel/agt`, a peer of `prj/` and `cfg/`. Unix has no convention for an interactive agent that runs as the user; `/opt`, `/var/lib` and `/srv` are for software and services under a service account. A dedicated Unix account per agent is the stronger boundary and stays in view for later.

## hv's calls

1. Harness state goes to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claude`. No `~/.claude` at all, no compat symlink: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is rendered from one value (`MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in the instance vars) into `zshenv` and the GUI environment path (a LaunchAgent `setenv` on macOS, `environment.d` on Linux), and `molt doctor` treats a reappeared `~/.claude` or `~/.claude.json` as the signal that a launch path missed the variable.
2. Config and runtime home are the same directory.
3. Roles `sysadm`, `ops`, `docs`; declared on rhadamanth, gyges and kovacs.
4. Enforcement: the home's `.claude/settings.json` is a fence the agent could edit; the root-owned managed-settings file is the wall. `ops` and `docs` get fence plus sandbox; `sysadm` gets a managed deny floor as its own work package (WP06).
5. No launch verb. `molt agent list` and `molt agent config <name>`. Claude only; Codex later, if ever.

## Facts verified (21 Oct)

- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates every `~/.claude` path, and also `~/.claude.json`: with the variable set to an empty directory, `claude config list` created `<dir>/.claude.json` (mode 600) and left `~/.claude.json` untouched. The docs do not say so; the test does.
- Settings precedence: managed, `--settings`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, user. `permissions.allow/deny/ask` merge across levels and deny wins at every level. Managed file: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json` (macOS), `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` (Linux), plus `managed-settings.d/`.
- `sandbox.enabled` stops sandboxed Bash from writing any `.claude` settings, hooks, shell rc files, `.git` config and the config dir, and no `allowWrite` entry or Edit allow rule lifts that. It binds sandboxed commands only: a command matching `sandbox.excludedCommands` runs with no filesystem restrictions and no network proxy; a command that fails in the sandbox may be retried unsandboxed on approval unless `sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` is `false`, which project settings may set; hooks, Edit and Write run outside it, and Edit and Write only prompt. So the `ops` and `docs` profiles set `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` and carry no `excludedCommands` (ac's reading of docs/sandboxing, verified by vc on 21 Oct).
- A `UserPromptSubmit` hook returning exit 2 blocks the prompt; Intent's in-session gate already uses it. The hook input's `cwd` follows Claude: it is the new directory after Claude runs `cd` in Bash, and the worktree root after it enters a worktree. `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, exported on the hook's process, is the directory the session started in and stays put. So the home-launch guard tests `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, never `cwd`, or a sleeve that started in its home and cd'd into `work/` would be blocked at its next prompt (dc's finding, verified on docs/hooks, 21 Oct).
- `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the launch directory even inside an enclosing git repository: a `claude -p` started in `repo/sub/deeper/` of a scratch repository, with a `UserPromptSubmit` hook recording the variable, got `repo/sub/deeper`, not the repository root (vc's probe, 21 Oct). So project settings, which load from the launch directory's `.claude/`, and the variable name the same directory, and a `$HOME` that is itself a git work tree (dotfiles) does not make the guard refuse launches below it.
- Project-scope settings (`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, their hooks and `autoMemoryDirectory`) load from the cwd's `.claude/` with no parent-directory fallback, while `CLAUDE.md` loads from the cwd and every directory above it (docs/permissions, docs/memory; ac's finding, verified by vc on 21 Oct). A sleeve started below its home, in `work/` say, keeps its contract and loses its fence, sandbox and memory setting. So the home-launch guard also refuses a session started under `MOLT_AGT_DIR` anywhere but in an agent home itself, and names the home to launch from (AC014): `cd <home>` is the launch, never a subdirectory; a `cd` inside a command afterwards is fine.
- Workspace trust: a home's `permissions.allow` rules wait for the trust dialog, which an interactive session shows once per directory (keyed on the directory outside a git repository, covering its subdirectories); a project-scope `autoMemoryDirectory` and hooks in settings files follow the same rule. A `claude -p` run never shows the dialog: it uses hooks and the memory setting but not the home's allow rules, and warns on stderr. Accepting the dialog at the first launch in each home is a WP04 step (docs/permissions, docs/memory).
- Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` natively (v2.1.277 or later) only when no `CLAUDE.md` sits in the cwd or above it; the home's one-line `CLAUDE.md` importing `@AGENTS.md` is the form that holds, and imports nest four hops deep (docs/memory).
- A live session cannot move its own state: `mv ~/.claude` under a running Claude moves its transcript, credentials and state out from under it. The move is run from a plain terminal with every Claude session on the host quit.
- `liberators/claude.sh` hardcodes `$HOME/.claude` in five places; the variable must be honoured before it is set anywhere.

## Constraints

- kovacs will be brew-only, and Molt itself will gain a brew install mode (hv, 21 Oct; not ready yet, and Molt on kovacs is a dev checkout for now). So: nothing in this thread may be anti-brew. Rendered files (the hook script, env files, GUI files, agent homes) reference no checkout path; what a sleeve agent needs at prompt time lives under `~/.config/molt/` or the agent home, where a brew-installed Molt will put it just the same.
- gyges is fixed later, not today (hv): its sleeve agent becomes `gyges-sysadm` when WP04 reaches it.
- Molt manages the user-scope `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` under the config dir as links from the user repo's `config/claude/` (hv, 21 Oct), so the cross-session rules are the same on every sleeve; kovacs lacked the Git Commits rule until 20 Oct while rhadamanth had it.
- Intent on rhadamanth is off limits (board watchout 16).
- Molt's CI runner is bash 3.2; run bats under `/bin/bash` too.
- No AI attribution in any commit; messages end `(C) hello@matthewsinclair.com`.
- Three Molt sessions share one checkout on rhadamanth: cc and dc work in git worktrees on `st0006-wp<NN>` branches; vc reviews and merges to main.
- `[[agent]]` entries land in the Molt-matts manifests only after WP02's parser is on every sleeve that reads them.

wps.title: Harness state leaves $HOME: claude liberator honours CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, renders it, moves once, refuses $HOME launches
wps.objective: Claude Code's state leaves $HOME on a sleeve that declares MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: the claude liberator honours CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, renders env.sh, the GUI file and the home-launch guard, moves ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json once with a clone backup, publishes the variable only once the state is in place, links the user-scope CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and reports through doctor; merged to main at 695e961 on 21 Oct.
wps.body:
Owner: molt-cc. Branch `st0006-wp01` in a git worktree; molt-vc reviews and merges.

## Contract

1. **One accessor for the config dir.** `molt_claude_config_dir` in `lib/molt.sh` answers `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}`; every `$HOME/.claude` in `liberators/claude.sh` (five today) goes through it. WP02's agents liberator uses the same accessor.
2. **One value, rendered twice, and it is the switch.** The sleeve's `instances/<host>/vars.sh` carries `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (the value hv declares in WP04 is `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/claude`). Everything this package adds (the move, the env file, the GUI file, the `$HOME` hook) runs only on a sleeve that declares it; an undeclared sleeve keeps today's behaviour plus the accessor and the 4a links. So merging WP01 changes no sleeve, and declaring the variable in a sleeve's vars.sh is how hv arms the move there, in WP04 (molt-cc's reading 1; on rhadamanth Chrome's native host keeps a `claude` process alive at all times, so an ungated move would refuse on every upgrade). The move targets the declared value, since under 3a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` cannot be set before it; once the state is in the declared dir, `claude_install` exports `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for the rest of the run so its links, statusLine and hook, and WP02's homes in the same resleeve, land there. Molt renders it into an env file the shell sources (`~/.config/molt/env.sh`, the pattern the iTerm2 ssh wrapper already uses) and into the GUI environment path: a LaunchAgent plist running `launchctl setenv CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` on macOS, `~/.config/environment.d/claude.conf` on Linux. Both carry `.molt-rendered` digest sidecars. `~/.zshenv` is a symlink into Molt-matts, not a render, so the value never appears in it as a literal; the zshenv line that sources the env file is Molt-matts work (WP03). On GNOME, `environment.d` reaches every GUI and terminal child; zshenv matters for ssh and TTY logins.
3. **The move, once.** When `$HOME/.claude` is a real directory and the config dir does not exist, `claude_install` backs up and moves `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` into place. It refuses, naming the processes, when any Claude Code is running (`pgrep -f`, never `pgrep -x`: board watchout 6), because a live session cannot survive its own state moving. It refuses a non-empty config dir, naming its contents, and never merges the two. `claude_install`'s `mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude"` (line 141 today) is the most dangerous of the five hardcoded sites: with the variable set it would recreate exactly what doctor faults.
3a. **The variable is published only once the state is where it points.** The env file and the GUI file are written only when the config dir holds the state (the move succeeded in this run, or `~/.claude` is already absent and the config dir present). When the move is refused for any reason, nothing is written in that run, in either dir: no env file, GUI file, link, statusLine or hook; the refusal says the variable was not published and `claude_install` returns 1, while resleeve carries on to the other liberators so an agent home still renders. Anything at all at `~/.claude` (file, dir or link) also refuses publication. The backup before the `mv` is a clone beside the target (`cp -cR` on APFS, `cp -a --reflink=auto` on Linux), never in `$HOME`. Otherwise the next Claude starts empty in the new dir (new login, new `.claude.json`) and the later move meets a non-empty target: split brain (kovacs-sysadm H1).
4. **Refuse `$HOME` launches.** A `UserPromptSubmit` hook, merged into the user `settings.json` the way the statusLine already is (generalise `_claude_statusline_install` into one merge-a-key function; Highlander), runs a script Molt renders into `~/.config/molt/`. The script reads the hook's JSON on stdin, and when `cwd` is `$HOME` exits 2 with "launch from an agent home: molt agent list". Any other cwd passes. The hook must not depend on `molt` being on PATH at prompt time.
4a. **User-scope rules, linked.** `_claude_links` gains `config/claude/CLAUDE.md` and `config/claude/AGENTS.md`, linked to `$(molt_claude_config_dir)/CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` when the user repo has them, as `keybindings.json` is today (hv, 21 Oct). An existing regular file there is backed up before the link, as `molt_link_all` already does; rhadamanth's current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is hv's richest copy and WP03 seeds the repo files from it, so the link must never land before the repo has the content (check reports the pending link; install makes it).
4b. **No checkout paths in anything rendered.** The hook script, env file and GUI file name only paths under `~/.config/molt/`, the config dir and `$HOME`; never `$MOLT_PRJ_DIR/Molt/...`. A brew-installed Molt (coming; hv) must produce byte-identical renders. The `.molt-rendered` sidecar's provenance line names the template path, as every sidecar does today; that is metadata nothing executes, and is allowed. The GUI file takes effect at the next login; Molt does not call `launchctl` or `systemctl`.
5. **Doctor.** `claude_check` reports: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset in the environment molt runs in; `~/.claude` or `~/.claude.json` present (file, dir or link) while the config dir is elsewhere, as the sign a launch path missed the variable; the env file, GUI file or hook missing or stale.

## Tests (bats, both bash 5 and `/bin/bash` 3.2)

Fake `$HOME` and fake config dir; a `pgrep` stub for the running-Claude refusal; a non-empty target refused and nothing merged; env and GUI files absent after any refusal and present after a successful move; the hook script run with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at `$HOME` (exit 2, message), elsewhere (exit 0), and unset (exit 1, blocks nothing); it reads no JSON and needs only sh; the merge function leaving every other settings key byte-identical (`jq -S` compare). No test may touch the real `~/.claude`.

## Out of scope

Codex. The compat symlink (hv: none). Moving any real sleeve (WP04).

wps.title: [[agent]] manifest table, MOLT_AGT_DIR and the agents liberator; molt agent list|config
wps.objective: Declare sleeve agents as `[[agent]]` tables in the sleeve's manifest, resolve one agents root (`MOLT_AGT_DIR`) through one validator, render each enabled agent's home (`AGENTS.md` from preamble, role and host overlay; `CLAUDE.md`; `.claude/settings.json`; `memory/`; `work/`) from the user repo's role, report and inspect them with `molt agent list` and `molt agent config`, and have the home-launch guard refuse a launch anywhere under the root that is not an agent home.
wps.body:
Owner: molt-cc. Branch `st0006-wp02` in a git worktree, on top of WP01; molt-vc reviews and merges.

## Contract

1. **Manifest.** `instances/<host>/molt.toml` gains `[[agent]]` tables: `role = "sysadm"` (required; one of the roles the user repo defines), `enabled = true` (default), `harness = "claude"` (default, the only value this thread accepts). The name is derived, never written: `<hostname>-<role>`, so the convention cannot be mistyped. The parser is the existing `[[liberator]]` one, generalised to take the table name (`_molt_liberator_entries` becomes one table parser; Highlander), and `test/manifest.bats` covers `[[agent]]` as it covers `[[liberator]]`.
2. **`MOLT_AGT_DIR`.** Default: the `agt/` sibling of `MOLT_PRJ_DIR`, computed exactly as Molt-matts' zshenv computes it (`${MOLT_PRJ_DIR:h}/agt`), defined where `MOLT_PRJ_DIR` and `MOLT_CFG_DIR` are, and that is the one resolver: a `vars.sh` that exports a different `MOLT_AGT_DIR` is refused, as is a root that is relative or untidy, or at or above `$HOME`, `MOLT_PRJ_DIR` or `MOLT_CFG_DIR` (one validator in `lib/agent.sh`, called by both liberators; critic-shell, 21 Oct). Exported from zshenv by Molt-matts (WP03). An agent's home is `$MOLT_AGT_DIR/<name>`.
3. **The `agents` liberator.** For each enabled agent, `agents_install` renders the home from the user repo's `config/agents/roles/<role>/`: `AGENTS.md` from three layers in order: the config repo's role-independent `config/agents/AGENTS.md.tmpl` when it has one (AC016: text common to every sleeve agent lives there and in no role template), the role's `AGENTS.md.tmpl`, and, when the sleeve has one, the instance overlay `instances/<host>/agents/<role>.md` (host facts that are true on this machine only: its stack layout, what is installed, known issues; the role template is one file for every host, so kovacs' "this VM, ext4, `~/mac`" cannot live in it: kovacs-sysadm), `CLAUDE.md` as the `@AGENTS.md` stub, `.claude/settings.json` from `settings.json.tmpl` with `autoMemoryDirectory` set to `<home>/memory`; creates `memory/` and `work/`. Rendering is Molt's `envsubst` with `MOLT_HOSTNAME`, `MOLT_AGENT_NAME`, `MOLT_AGENT_ROLE`, `MOLT_AGENT_HOME` available; `.molt-rendered` digest sidecars decide re-rendering, as for ssh. `memory/` and `work/` are the agent's and are never written by Molt after creation. A role the user repo does not define is a fault naming the role and the path looked in. Rendering a home does not depend on the harness state having moved (WP01): the first `molt upgrade` on kovacs renders the home while kovacs-sysadm is still live and WP01's move is refused, so that it can copy its files in before hv runs the move (kovacs-sysadm H2). `agents_check` and `agents_verify` report missing or stale homes; `agents_upgrade` re-renders stale ones.
4. **`molt agent list`** prints each declared agent: name, role, home, enabled, and whether its rendered files are current. **`molt agent config <name>`** prints the home, the role, each rendered file's currency, and the effective permissions: `permissions.allow/deny/ask` merged from the managed file, the user settings and the home's `.claude/settings.json`, each rule tagged with the layer it came from. An undeclared name fails and lists the declared ones.
5. **The home-launch guard's second rule (AC014).** WP01's `claude-home-guard.sh.tmpl` gains, with the resolved `MOLT_AGT_DIR` rendered in as a literal: a session whose `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` lies under `MOLT_AGT_DIR` without being an agent home itself (the agents root, or anything below a home) is refused, naming the home to launch from; a session started exactly in a home passes. The claude liberator exports the resolved root for its renders and refuses to render the hook with a missing or relative one, and doctor compares the root baked into the rendered hook with the resolved one, reporting a mismatch as "re-run molt upgrade" (the install re-renders, so that is true).

## Tests

Fake user repo with a role dir; fake `$MOLT_AGT_DIR`; render, re-render no-op, stale after the template changes or the instance overlay changes; render with and without an overlay; undefined role fault; derived name; `agent config` merging three fake settings layers and tagging each rule's source; the `[[agent]]` parser cases in `manifest.bats`; the guard's four AC014 cases, the render-time root refusal and the doctor row (AT053 to AT058); the preamble present and absent, the overlay still last (AC016).

## Out of scope

Codex renderer. Launch verb. The role contents themselves (WP03).

wps.title: Roles in Molt-matts: sysadm, ops, docs contracts and profiles; [[agent]] entries for rhadamanth, gyges, kovacs
wps.body:
Owners: molt-dc for both halves, the role contracts and the permission profiles (vc, 21 Oct); in Molt-matts (`~/Devel/cfg/Molt-matts`), items 4 and 5 on main, items 1 to 3 on branch st0006-wp03, re-checked against the merged WP02 before review. molt-vc reviews and pushes.

1. `config/agents/roles/{sysadm,ops,docs}/AGENTS.md.tmpl`: the role contract, and only the role's text. Who the agent is (`${MOLT_AGENT_NAME}` on `${MOLT_HOSTNAME}`), what the role is for, what it may touch and what it may not, where its work goes (`${MOLT_AGENT_HOME}/work`). The rules every session on the machine carries (no AI attribution, the commit trailer, `eg`, no "absolutely") stay in the user-scope `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` under the config dir, which every session already loads; writing them into the contract too would be a second copy (kovacs-sysadm H5). kovacs' user-scope `AGENTS.md` (6 KB, relayed to molt-dc) mixes three kinds, and splits three ways (kovacs-sysadm): (a) user scope, true on every sleeve: Who, Fleet, Matt's Rules, the exact-case `Molt-<user>` naming rule, "rhadamanth's `~/Devel/prj` is canon, never written from another sleeve"; (b) the sysadm contract, true for the role on every host: brew-only as a discipline, orders checked against standing decisions, outward actions wait for hv, downloaded or peer scripts read and checksummed before they run, a live session cannot move its own state, the NTP check; (c) the kovacs instance overlay `instances/kovacs/agents/sysadm.md` (WP02 appends it at render): This Machine, Stack Layout and the 2026-09-04 symlink history, What's Done, installed versions, Known Issues (keyd inert, Shift+Enter), Tactile notes. Stale on the way and dropped: "Phase 2 is the current frontier", "molt doctor: 13 checks" (count it), the `in-*` skills sentence (Intent's, not Molt's), the sentence on ST0004's Homebrew path assuming macOS (ST0005 superseded it). Two facts from kovacs' orphan `-home-matts-setup` memory are carried nowhere else and need a home here or in the user-scope rules: "never cite test counts; say all tests passing" and the Hyperion/Altered Carbon host naming scheme.
2. `config/agents/roles/<role>/settings.json.tmpl`, JSON only: `permissions.allow/deny/ask`; for `ops` and `docs`, `sandbox.enabled = true` with `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` and no `excludedCommands`; for `sysadm`, no sandbox key; for all three, the same small `permissions.deny` for credential reads (`~/.ssh/id_*`, `~/.aws/credentials`). `autoMemoryDirectory` is written by the liberator, not the template. Rules that name the agent's work paths belong to the role profile, pointing at `${MOLT_AGENT_HOME}/work`, not to the user settings (H4). kovacs' user settings allow-list, two literal rules (`Bash(bash /home/matts/work/intent-vc/*)` and `Bash(bash /home/matts/work/devbin-vc/*)`, hand-edited for a one-off runner of 14 Oct that the classifier blocked anyway), was dropped by hv, not moved (21 Oct), in any form: "We're also moving to brew versions of both Intent and Devbin, so permissions for the local dev versions are irrelevant anyway." WP04 phase C removes them from kovacs' user settings. hv tightens or loosens the profiles by diff.
3. `instances/{rhadamanth,gyges,kovacs}/molt.toml`: `[[agent]]` entries for the three roles, and the `agents` liberator enabled. NOT `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: declaring it in a sleeve's vars.sh arms WP01's move on that sleeve's next upgrade, so it is declared per sleeve in WP04, by hv, when that sleeve is ready to move. Homes render without it.
4. `config/zsh/zshenv`: export `MOLT_AGT_DIR` beside `MOLT_PRJ_DIR`, and `[ -r ~/.config/molt/env.sh ] && . ~/.config/molt/env.sh`. The line can land before WP01 is on a sleeve, since it sources nothing until the file exists, and it must be there before the move runs.
5. `config/claude/CLAUDE.md` and `config/claude/AGENTS.md`: the user-scope rules every sleeve's sessions load, linked into the config dir by WP01 4a. Seed `CLAUDE.md` from rhadamanth's current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (hv's richest copy: Global Rules, Elixir, Tone and Style; the Git Commits rule is identical on kovacs) and `AGENTS.md` from part (a) of the kovacs split plus the two carried facts (test counts, host naming). Before the link lands on a sleeve, diff that sleeve's live file against the repo copy so nothing hv wrote locally is lost; a difference is folded into the repo first.

Done when `molt doctor` is green on rhadamanth with the three homes rendered, and the Molt-matts commits are pushed.

wps.title: Move kovacs-sysadm into its home; then rhadamanth, then gyges
wps.objective: Move each sleeve, kovacs first, then rhadamanth, then gyges on hv's date, so that Claude Code's state sits in the sleeve's declared config dir with none of it left in `$HOME`, and its sysadm agent runs from its own home with its memory there, following the runbook below, which hv executes at the keyboard.
wps.body:
## How this runs

Owner: kovacs-sysadm plans and verifies kovacs; hv executes each move at the keyboard; molt-vc reviews. molt-ac wrote these steps down on 21 Oct from three sources: kovacs-sysadm's plan, whose phase A and C specifics vc relayed; the merged claude liberator, `liberators/claude.sh` and `templates/claude/` (main at c815d23); and dc's guide, `docs/guides/sleeve-agents.md`, on branch `st0006-wp05` until it merges. The guide explains the mechanism, and this runbook names its sections rather than repeating them. vc checked every quoted molt line against the code.

No agent can move its own state: `mv ~/.claude` under a running session moves its transcript, credentials and state out from under it. So each sleeve moves in three phases. In A, the sleeve's agent, still live, copies what it keeps into its new home. In B, hv, at a plain terminal with no Claude running, declares the config dir and runs the move. In C, the agent, in a new session started in its home, verifies and cleans up. Until C3, the first deletion, everything can be rolled back from the backup the move takes (see Rollback).

kovacs-sysadm's plan and verify script start on kovacs at `~/work/ST0006-WP04-move-plan.md` and `~/work/verify-wp04.sh`, and A2 copies them into the home. Their dry run on 21 Oct gave AC008 FAIL, as expected before the move, with `molt doctor` already green. H4, H5 and H6 below are the plan's labels.

How molt's output is quoted here: molt prefixes its lines `Zen:`, its warnings `Zen [warning]:` and its errors `Zen [error]:`. `<stamp>` is `YYYYmmddHHMMSS` in local time, the declared config dir is `~/.config/claude`, and `/home/matts` is kovacs' home directory. In kovacs' steps, `h` is kovacs-sysadm's home: `h=~/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm`.

## Before any sleeve

**P1. The code is merged and pushed.** WP02 in Molt: the agents liberator, `molt agent list` and `molt agent config`, and the guard's refusal below a home (AC014). WP03 in Molt-matts: the roles, kovacs' sysadm overlay and the `[[agent]]` entries (branch `st0006-wp03`, at 769c2e6 when this was written). The `[[agent]]` entries reach a sleeve only once WP02's parser is on it.

**P2. Intent follows the move.** From 3.2.4 (issue 0604), Intent reads `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: `intent claude skills` and `subagents`, the prompt gate and `/in-session` look where it points, so the skills under `~/.claude/skills/` move with the state and are found there. kovacs runs Intent 3.2.4 from Homebrew. The move does not touch Intent itself, which on rhadamanth is off limits.

**P3. The time is hv's.** hv picks when each sleeve moves, once vc has reviewed this runbook.

**P4. A dirty checkout stops `molt upgrade`.** Every `molt upgrade` in this runbook, `--self` included, first checks the sleeve's Molt and Molt-matts checkouts, and refuses while either has staged or unstaged changes to tracked files: `Zen [error]: Framework repo has uncommitted changes. Commit or stash before upgrading.`, or the same with `User config`. Nothing has run: commit or stash, then run the step again. Untracked files and unpushed commits only warn.

**P5. After a pull that changes Molt's code, upgrade in a fresh command.** `molt` sources its library when it starts, and an upgrade that pulls re-sources only its constants, so the liberators it has just pulled can call library functions the running process never loaded (issue 0023). The first `molt upgrade` after pulling WP02 ends `Liberator failed: claude`, `Liberator failed: agents` and `Zen [error]: 2 liberator(s) failed. Review errors above.`, and renders no home; a second run works. So pull with `molt upgrade --self`, then run `molt upgrade` as a second command. B2 then B5 in one sitting already does this.

## kovacs

### Phase A: kovacs-sysadm, live, copies only

Nothing in A declares the variable or touches `~/.claude`, so kovacs-sysadm's session stays whole. kovacs-sysadm runs its plan's phase A; these are its steps.

**A1. Render the homes.** kovacs-sysadm or hv runs, on kovacs, as two commands (P5):

```bash
molt upgrade --self
molt upgrade
```

With `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` not declared, the claude liberator moves nothing, and the agents liberator renders `~/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm`, `kovacs-ops` and `kovacs-docs`. The claude liberator also links the user-scope `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` from Molt-matts' `config/claude/` (660a118, which kovacs has not pulled yet), backing up kovacs' own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` as `.molt-backup.<stamp>`, so a backup line in this run's output is expected. The run should end:

```
Zen: Sleeve ready. Welcome back.
```

Then check the home:

```bash
h=~/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm
molt agent list
ls -d "$h/AGENTS.md" "$h/CLAUDE.md" "$h/.claude/settings.json" "$h/memory" "$h/work"
jq -r .autoMemoryDirectory "$h/.claude/settings.json"
```

`molt agent list` shows kovacs-sysadm with STATE `current` and HOME `~/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm` (guide: "Listing and inspecting agents"); `ls` finds all five; `jq` prints `/home/matts/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm/memory`.

If it refuses, a dirty checkout is P4's case, and two `Liberator failed` lines with no home rendered are P5's: run `molt upgrade` again. An `agents:` report is a row of the guide's "What molt doctor reports" and is WP02's or WP03's to fix: stop and tell vc.

**A2. Copy into the home**, leaving every original in place until C3. kovacs-sysadm's commands, verbatim:

```bash
cp -a ~/.claude/projects/-home-matts/memory/. "$h/memory/"
rsync -a --exclude=/tmp/ ~/work/ "$h/work/"
cp -a ~/prov "$h/work/prov"
mkdir -p "$h/work/archive/projects"
cp -a ~/.claude/projects/-home-matts-work-o7h-proj ~/.claude/projects/-home-matts-setup "$h/work/archive/projects/"
```

So the memory lands in `$h/memory/`, which the home's settings name as `autoMemoryDirectory`. `~/work`'s contents land in `$h/work/`: the FOLD note, `intent-vc/`, `devbin-vc/`, the empty `utilz-vc/`, `order2.sh`, `order2.log`, and the plan and verify script, at `$h/work/ST0006-WP04-move-plan.md` and `$h/work/verify-wp04.sh`. `intent-vc/` and `devbin-vc/` are not checkouts: they hold order scripts, logs and `.rc` files from 14-17 Oct. `~/prov` lands in `$h/work/prov/`, and the two slugs, `-home-matts-work-o7h-proj` (three transcripts and its memory) and `-home-matts-setup` (one `MEMORY.md` from 2026-03-10, stale Phase 1 notes, whose two live facts Molt-matts' user-scope `AGENTS.md` already carries), under `$h/work/archive/projects/`. `~/work/tmp/` is left out: it holds hv's `doom-rebuild.log`, which hv does not need kept, so it goes with `~/work` at C3.

**A3. Point the memory at the home.** Two lines in `$h/memory/kovacs-sysadm-role.md` name `~/work`, and they are the only ones in the memory; find them by their text, since line numbers drift if the memory changes before A2. In the line reading "Read ~/work/FOLD-kovacs-sysadm.md first", the path becomes `$h/work/FOLD-kovacs-sysadm.md`. The bullet quoting the allow rule hv dropped is reworded. Left alone, the verify script fails with "memory still names ~/work".

**A4. Compare each copy with its source** before folding:

```bash
diff -r ~/.claude/projects/-home-matts/memory "$h/memory"
diff -r ~/work "$h/work"
diff -r ~/prov "$h/work/prov"
diff -r ~/.claude/projects/-home-matts-work-o7h-proj "$h/work/archive/projects/-home-matts-work-o7h-proj"
diff -r ~/.claude/projects/-home-matts-setup "$h/work/archive/projects/-home-matts-setup"
```

The only differences expected are A3's two lines, `tmp` only in `~/work`, and `prov` and `archive` only in `$h/work`, the other copies.

**A5. Fold and quit.** kovacs-sysadm's fold writes `$h/work/FOLD-kovacs-sysadm.md`; the originals in `~/work` are not edited after A2. Then it quits. From here no Claude Code runs on kovacs until B9.

### Phase B: hv, at a plain terminal, with no Claude running

**B1. Declare the config dir.** In Molt-matts on main, add to `instances/kovacs/vars.sh`:

```bash
export MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/claude"
```

Commit, ending the message `(C) hello@matthewsinclair.com`, and push. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset on kovacs, so the value is `/home/matts/.config/claude`; B3 shows what molt reads. This arms the move: the next `molt upgrade` or `molt resleeve` on kovacs runs it.

**B2. Pull on kovacs**, without resleeving (P4 applies):

```bash
molt upgrade --self
```

**B3. Check the declaration arrived:**

```bash
molt doctor
```

Its enabled-liberators step must report the pending move. Doctor puts the liberator's name before each report, so `claude:` appears twice:

```
         not installed: claude
         claude: Zen: claude: Claude Code's state is still in ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json, and this sleeve's config dir is ~/.config/claude: quit every Claude Code, then run molt resleeve to move it
```

`not installed` may name other liberators as well. Anything else in claude's report means stop; nothing has changed yet:

- a line naming `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, eg `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not a canonical path, with no trailing slash, // or . or .. component: <path>`: fix B1's line, push, and repeat from B2;
- `~/.claude and ~/.claude.json are present while the config dir is ~/.config/claude: a launch path missed CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or a move did not finish`: `~/.config/claude` already holds something, which the move will not merge with; tell vc and kovacs-sysadm;
- no claude report at all: the declaration did not arrive; check that B2 pulled Molt-matts.

**B4. Quit every Claude Code on kovacs**: every terminal session, kovacs-sysadm's included, and any started from the GUI. The move checks for itself and names any it finds. To look first:

```bash
pgrep -fa '^([^ ]*/)?claude( |$)|@anthropic-ai/claude-code'
```

On a Mac the same pattern goes to `pgrep -afl`, since macOS's `pgrep` leaves out its own ancestors without `-a`.

**B5. Run the move:**

```bash
molt upgrade
```

Claude's part of the resleeve prints these lines in this order, among molt's other lines:

```
Zen: claude: Claude Code's state is still in ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json, and this sleeve's config dir is ~/.config/claude: quit every Claude Code, then run molt resleeve to move it
Zen: Running liberator: claude (install)
Zen: claude: moved Claude Code's state into ~/.config/claude; the copies taken first are in ~/.config/claude.molt-backup.<stamp>
Zen [warning]: claude: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not ~/.config/claude in this shell. Start Claude Code only from a new shell that sources ~/.config/molt/env.sh, and log out and in for apps started from the GUI
Zen [warning]: Backing up existing file: /home/matts/.config/claude/settings.json -> /home/matts/.config/claude/settings.json.molt-backup.<stamp>
Zen: claude: home-launch hook written into ~/.config/claude/settings.json
Zen: Liberator complete: claude
  claude: ✓ installed
```

The run should end `Zen: Sleeve ready. Welcome back.` The first line is the check reporting the pending move, just before the install carries it out. The first warning is expected, because this shell started before `env.sh` existed. If the statusLine changed too, a second backup line and `Zen: claude: statusLine written into ~/.config/claude/settings.json` come before the hook's. Note the backup's path: the rollback starts from it.

If it refuses, the refusal ends with a `Zen [error]: claude: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR was not published` line and `Zen [error]: Liberator failed: claude`, and the run ends `Zen [error]: 1 liberator(s) failed. Review errors above.` The other liberators still run, the agent homes among them. By the first error line:

- `Zen [error]: claude: Claude Code is running, and a live session cannot survive its own state moving:`, then one `Zen [error]:   <pid> <command>` line per process, then `Zen [error]: claude: quit every Claude Code on this machine, then run molt resleeve from a plain terminal`: nothing moved. Quit each process named and run B5 again; `molt resleeve`, which the line names, runs the same move.
- `Zen [error]: claude: pgrep could not list processes, so whether Claude Code is running is unknown`: nothing moved. Run B5 again, and if it repeats, stop and tell vc.
- a line containing `already holds`, `is a symlink to`, `both exist`, `holds nothing, and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR named` or `is not a`, with the not-published line ending `and nothing else was changed`: nothing moved. Stop and tell vc and kovacs-sysadm, and change nothing by hand until they have looked; the guide's "What the move does, and when it refuses" says what each means.
- a line naming the copies, `the copies are in ~/.config/claude.molt-backup.<stamp>`, with the not-published line ending `no env.sh or GUI file was written`: the move failed after the copying began. If the line says `nothing was moved`, the state is still in `$HOME`: deal with the cause it names, then run B5 again. If it says the state `is split`, start no Claude: either move `~/.claude.json` to `~/.config/claude/.claude.json` by hand, as the line says, or roll back. Tell vc either way.
- P4's dirty-checkout line, with no claude line after it: nothing ran, and P4 says what to do.

**B6. Check from a new shell.** Open a new terminal:

```bash
echo "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"
ls -d ~/.claude ~/.claude.json
ls -A ~/.config/claude.molt-backup.<stamp>
```

The first prints `/home/matts/.config/claude`; the second finds neither; the third lists `.claude` and `.claude.json`, the copies a rollback needs.

**B7. Log out of GNOME and back in**, so every GUI and terminal child gets the variable from `~/.config/environment.d/claude.conf` (plan H6). Molt does not call `systemctl`; the file takes effect at login.

**B8. Check the sleeve:**

```bash
molt doctor
```

The enabled-liberators step should name no claude report. A `claude:` line there is a row of the guide's "What molt doctor reports", which says what to do.

**B9. Launch kovacs-sysadm from its home**, by name, so peers and `ListAgents` see it:

```bash
cd ~/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm && claude --name kovacs-sysadm
```

Accept the workspace trust dialog: the home's allow rules, its hooks and its `autoMemoryDirectory` wait for it (guide: "Starting an agent"). If Claude Code asks you to log in, log in. The first prompt passes the home-launch guard, because the session started in a home.

### Phase C: kovacs-sysadm, in its new session

**C1. Verify.** kovacs-sysadm runs, from its home:

```bash
work/verify-wp04.sh c1
```

AC008 should now pass: kovacs-sysadm runs from `~/Devel/agt/kovacs-sysadm` with its memory in the home, and `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` are gone from `$HOME`. At `c1` the script reports C3's items as INFO; it reads `AGENT` from the environment, defaulting to kovacs-sysadm. Then the session states its role memory without reading a file: the proof that `autoMemoryDirectory` and the trust dialog took effect, not only that the files exist. The new session has a new session id, so its bridge address has changed: kovacs-sysadm sends the new one to molt-vc, intent-vc and devbin-vc. If anything fails, stop here, while the rollback is still whole.

**C2. hv's word.** kovacs-sysadm removes nothing until hv says so. From C3 on, a rollback still puts Claude Code's state back from the backup, but `~/work` and `~/prov` come back only from their copies in the home.

**C3. Remove, on hv's word:**

- `~/work` and `~/prov`, both copied into the home in A2; `~/work/tmp/doom-rebuild.log`, which A2 left out, goes with them (hv: not needed);
- the whole `~/.config/claude/projects/-home-matts` slug, kovacs-sysadm's old transcripts and its `memory/`, a stale second copy of the home's memory after A2 (hv: remove the whole folder);
- the orphan slugs A2 archived, `-home-matts-work-o7h-proj` and `-home-matts-setup` (per kovacs-sysadm's plan, relayed by vc), from `~/.config/claude/projects/`, where the move put them;
- the two user-scope allow rules hv dropped, `Bash(bash /home/matts/work/intent-vc/*)` and `Bash(bash /home/matts/work/devbin-vc/*)` (verbatim from kovacs-sysadm, relayed by vc), from `~/.config/claude/settings.json` (plan H4); both point into the `~/work` this step removes;
- the npm-era leftovers `~/.cache/claude-cli-nodejs` and `~/.npm` (hv: kill).

The user-scope `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in `~/.config/claude` are by now links into Molt-matts' `config/claude/` (plan H5) and need nothing.

**C4. Verify again:** `work/verify-wp04.sh c4`, which requires C3's items gone, then `molt doctor`, which should name no claude or agents report.

**C5. Fold.** kovacs-sysadm folds.

Left alone throughout: `~/tmp`, which is root-owned and holds hv's handover note; and the native installer's own paths, `~/.local/bin/claude`, `~/.local/share/claude`, `~/.local/state/claude` and `~/.cache/claude`, which `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does not move and which are not clutter. Molt never removes the backup.

## Rollback

From the backup the move took, for anything before C3, or for a move that stopped part way. Quit every Claude first, as in B4.

**R1. Disarm.** Take the `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` line out of `instances/<host>/vars.sh`, commit and push, then on the sleeve run `molt upgrade --self`. While the line stands, the next `molt upgrade` tries the move again.

**R2. Unpublish.** Once a sleeve declares nothing, molt leaves these files as they are, and `env.sh` would go on exporting the variable to every zsh. On kovacs:

```bash
rm ~/.config/molt/env.sh ~/.config/molt/env.sh.molt-rendered
rm ~/.config/molt/claude-home-guard.sh ~/.config/molt/claude-home-guard.sh.molt-rendered
rm ~/.config/environment.d/claude.conf ~/.config/environment.d/claude.conf.molt-rendered
```

On a Mac, `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.molt.claude-config-dir.plist` and its `.molt-rendered` take the place of the `environment.d` pair.

**R3. Put the state back** from the backup B5 named. Set the moved dir aside rather than deleting it, since it holds whatever ran after the move:

```bash
b=~/.config/claude.molt-backup.<stamp>
mv ~/.config/claude ~/.config/claude.rolled-back
cp -a --reflink=auto "$b/.claude" "$b/.claude.json" ~/
```

On a Mac the copy is `cp -cRp "$b/.claude" "$b/.claude.json" ~/`, an APFS clone. A move that stopped part way may have left `~/.claude` or `~/.claude.json` in `$HOME`: set it aside the same way before the copy. The backup's `settings.json` predates the hook, so the restored user settings carry none.

**R4. Log out and back in**, so no GUI app keeps the variable. Then, in a new shell, `echo "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR-unset}"` prints `unset`.

**R5. Check and report.** `molt doctor` should name no claude report about a config dir, since the sleeve declares none. Tell vc. The set-aside dir stays until hv decides what becomes of it. The home and the copies in it stay too, and `molt agent list` still shows kovacs-sysadm `current`, with a home nobody launches from.

## rhadamanth

After kovacs has passed C4, the same three phases, with these differences:

- A: the first upgrade after WP02 and WP03 is two commands, as in A1 (P5), and renders `~/Devel/agt/rhadamanth-sysadm`, `rhadamanth-ops` and `rhadamanth-docs`. Then hv copies the memory of the sessions launched in `$HOME`, which are sysadm memories, into rhadamanth-sysadm's home, and confirms the destination: `cp -Rp ~/.claude/projects/-Users-matts/memory/. ~/Devel/agt/rhadamanth-sysadm/memory/`. vc's inventory on 21 Oct found `MEMORY.md` and four notes there (doom-emacs-version-profile-miss, emacs-plus31-dylib-crash, launchd-agents-tcc-network-volumes, nas-smb-share-wedges-emfile), so `ls ~/Devel/agt/rhadamanth-sysadm/memory/` should list those. The slug's one session transcript stays where it is, and moves with the state.
- B1: the line goes in `instances/rhadamanth/vars.sh`, with the same value, which here is `/Users/matts/.config/claude`.
- B2: skip it when B1's commit is made in rhadamanth's own Molt-matts checkout, the one molt reads. B5: P4's refusal is the likely one here, because the shared Molt checkout usually has uncommitted board files. Every session's fold commits its own board before B4, so that `git status` in both checkouts shows no modified or staged file when B5 runs.
- B4 quits every Claude Code on the machine, which on rhadamanth is every session hv runs: molt-vc, molt-cc, molt-dc and molt-ac, and every other project's, such as geodica-vc. Each folds first. Quit Chrome as well: while it runs with the extension, its native host (`~/.local/bin/claude --chrome-native-host`) is a `claude` process, and B5 refuses on it. Quit the Claude desktop app if it is open.
- B5: the lines are kovacs' with `/Users/matts` for `/home/matts`. `~/.claude` is about 9G, and the backup is an APFS clone (`cp -cRp`), so it costs next to no space.
- B7: the GUI file is `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.molt.claude-config-dir.plist`, which runs `/bin/launchctl setenv CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at login, so this step is a macOS log out and in.
- B9 and C: each agent starts from its home, and each project session from its project, with the transcripts and memory that moved with the state. What C removes on rhadamanth is the inventory's to say.

## gyges

Later, on a date hv sets, and through gyges-infra, whose sleeve agent becomes `gyges-sysadm` when WP04 reaches it. gyges is a Mac, so rhadamanth's differences apply, and gyges-infra inventories its phase A.

## Not decided here

WP06's deny floor for sysadm, which is hv's; gyges' date; and when each backup and each set-aside dir is removed. Until hv says, each stays. That includes three Molt backups A1 left in kovacs' `~/.claude`, which B5 carries into `~/.config/claude` and C3 does not remove: `AGENTS.md.molt-backup.20261021183245` and `CLAUDE.md.molt-backup.20261021183245`, made when A1 linked the user-scope files over kovacs' own, and `settings.json.molt-backup.20261020230015`, from 20 Oct.

wps.title: Managed deny floor for sysadm
wps.body:
Owner: molt-cc, after WP01 to WP05. molt-vc reviews.

The `sysadm` role cannot be sandboxed, so its home's deny list is a fence the agent could edit. This package renders the role's `permissions.deny` into the root-owned managed-settings file (`/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.d/molt-sysadm.json` on macOS, `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.d/molt-sysadm.json` on Linux), through the sudo path the `system` liberator already uses, with a digest sidecar beside it. `molt agent config <name>` already tags each rule's layer, so a managed rule shows as managed. `molt doctor` reports the floor missing or stale. hv decides the floor's contents; the mechanism is this package.

wps.title: Blog brief: so you want to run a local agent (precis, structure, bullets; hv writes the piece)
wps.objective: A precis, an audience statement, a structure and bullets per section for hv's blog post on running a local agent: notes hv writes the piece from, not the piece.
wps.body:
Owner: molt-ac. Written on main, in the main checkout, no branch and no worktree: hv, 21 Oct, "Just edit in docs/blog directly." molt-ac commits its own path; molt-vc reviews the committed file on main against AC013. (The branch `st0006-wp07` carried the first draft, dd041b6, and was deleted as superseded.) hv, 21 Oct: "I don't want it to write the piece, I want to do that, but what I want is a precis/brief, a structure, and then some bullet points per section."

Deliverable: `docs/blog/bl0001-so-you-want-to-run-a-local-agent.md`, the working notes for a blog post hv will write. Title to be worked out ("Organising a Local Agent" is one candidate). It holds: a precis (what the piece argues, in a paragraph), the audience statement, the structure as sections, and three to eight bullets per section: the points to make, the examples to reach for, the facts to check. Not prose, not the piece.

The narrative arc, hv's:

1. So you want to run an agent on your machine.
2. Why is that a good thing?
3. What are the risks of doing this?
4. What are some good ways to manage these risks?
5. How do I set up and configure the agent?
6. What if I have multiple different (scoped) things I want my agent(s) to do?
7. What if I have multiple machines?
8. Who is this advice for? Compare and contrast "just use the agent app" at one extreme (this piece is not for you) with "I run tens of coding agents in multiple swarms simultaneously and know what I am doing" at the other.
